messages:
maya: quick q — onboarding a community model (cumulus-7b) that has a weird clause. License text says 'weights may be redistributed for non-commercial research only; derivatives must include attribution to upstream and not be offered as a service that generates revenue.' Can we ship quantized weights inside a Docker image we hand to Dedicated/private customers?

ian: short answer: probably a no for paid hosting. 'not be offered as a service that generates revenue' sounds like an NC/service restriction. But need exact wording. Do we have the full license file?

sophie: i pulled the repo and the LICENSE.txt is a custom short form. snippet: "Weights and derived binaries may be redistributed for research only; commercial hosting or sale prohibited." — no SPDX id.

maya: yup that's the one. Our use case: 1) Hosted API (not allowed if commercial) 2) Dedicated/reserved customers where we ship an image containing the quantized model to run in their VPC (they pay us/reserved contract) 3) Private on-prem install we deliver as an appliance (customer has infra). Which of these are blocked?

legal: tagging @legal — quick surface guidance: "research only" + explicit prohibition on commercial hosting means we cannot offer the model as part of a paid hosted API. For Dedicated/private we need to determine whether 'redistribute' covers delivering weights to paying customers. Likely yes — if we physically include weights in a container we are redistributing the weights.

license-bot: NOTE: custom licenses without clear SPDX require human review. Potential risky clauses: 'not be offered as a service' ~ service-use restriction; 'research only' ~ noncommercial.

tomas: follow-up: does quantization produce a "derivative" under copyright? e.g., q8_0 weights are transformed tensors — is that derivative work or just a transform? Upstream might claim derivative.

legal: many licensors consider quantized weights as derivative or at least a transformed artifact; courts not super settled. We should treat quantization as a derivative for policy. So if original license restricts usage or redistribution, those restrictions likely apply to quantized versions too.

devops: operationally, if redistribution is blocked we could instead host model blobs in a private object store and stream to customer infra at runtime (if contractual rights allow hosting without redistributing binaries). But that still looks like offering a service if customers pay.

ian: another option: ship a thin image that contains only code and a downloader step so the customer pulls the model from upstream (if upstream allows direct customer download). That shifts redistribution to the customer. But requires upstream to have a public download or give per-customer access.

liz: note: some customers require an offline appliance where we pre-bake everything. For those cases, we need explicit redistribution permission or a separate licensing agreement.

maya: ok, actionable next steps? I can pause onboarding until we have clarity. We started evals/quant runs locally (no external distribution yet).

legal: action items: 1) @sophie to capture exact license text and file it in legal tracker (CLA-1234). 2) @sophie please ask upstream maintainers for explicit redistribution rights for: a) shipping quantized weights inside a container to paying customers, b) permitting commercial hosting. Ask for a commercial license or an exception. 3) until we have confirmation, mark model as NOT_FOR_HOSTED in onboarding tracker and restrict Dedicated/Private packaging.

sophie: filing now, will ping upstream asking for a commercial license / redistribution addendum. Draft message: "we're evaluating Cumulus-7B; repo LICENSE restricts redistribution to research-only. Our enterprise use case includes delivering container images and on-prem appliances to customers under contract. Would you consider granting a commercial redistribution exception or selling a commercial license?" LMK edits.

legal: draft looks fine. add: 'we will not publish weights publicly or reupload to model hubs until we have written consent.'

license-bot: Suggested interim policy: flag model as: "ONBOARDING: redistribute? NO; hosted? NO; private appliance? REQUIRES EXCEPTION" — update trackers accordingly.

maya: thanks. also question on attribution: the license requires conspicuous attribution + link to original paper. If upstream agrees to an exception, can we include attribution in the Docker / ABOUT file and in our Console UI?

legal: yes — attribution in container / README + customer-facing UI is ok. Keep exact attribution text they require. Save a copy of any required notices into /legal/third_party_notices. We'll automate injection into images when granted.

tomas: small tech note for devs: if we get permission to redistribute only the quantized weights but NOT the original float weights, make sure artifact names and provenance record that — otherwise downstream audits confuse originals vs quantized. Add a model-card field: `redistribution_allowed: quantized_only`

devops: implementation approaches: a) host model artifact in our private registry and let images pull at build-time (requires legal ok) b) bundle at build-time -> larger image but easier offline installs c) provide build script and let customer obtain weights from upstream (preferred if allowed).

maya: ok i'll pause packaging. @sophie can you drop the upstream response here once you get it and i'll update the evals dashboard (we're tracking quality/regressions vs hf/float baseline).

liz: FYI: for customers who already signed enterprise contracts, check the contract language — some contracts allow us to ship third-party binaries under customer responsibility. Legal to review per-customer.

sophie: pinged upstream (sent email + GH issue). Will paste replies. ETA 48h.

maya: great — thanks everyone. I'll document current blocking status in the model onboarding board and remove hosted/Dedicated packaging until clarified. :white_check_mark:
